newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Autonomy for S.African tax body in Q2 - Manuel.
newsitem.headline: Autonomy for S.African tax body in Q2 - Manuel.

text.p: Legislation paving the way for the full autonomy of a revamped South African Revenue Services would probably only be ready in the second quarter of this year, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Friday.

Answering questions in parliament, Manuel said that he would probably not be able to keep his promise to have the legislation passed in the first quarter because of the complexities encountered in drafting the legislation.
"Probably by the end of the second quarter it probably would have been tabled and dealt with by parliament," he said.
For example, he said, some staff members were currently employed by the public service and would have to be employed by a different and new organisation.
"What do you do with the pension funds? How is that reflected in the legislation?" he asked.

The new tax body is seeking full autonomy so that it can pay professional staff the market related salaries it cannot pay as part of the civil service. This is seen as vital for it to be able to attract the skills needed to overhaul the tax collection system.
Manuel said that it was still too early to judge the success of the latest tax amnesty, which expires on February 28, but that he expected a lot of last minute applications.
"We expect a deluge of letters and cheques in the course of next week as people come in on the right side," he said. -- Parliamentary office +27 21 403-2502
